item.title: Workplace Learning for Sustainable Professional Development: Formal, Informal, and Evolving Learning Practices
item.content:encoded:
Cataldo Giuliano Gemmano, University of Bari Aldo Moro

Maria Luisa Giancaspro, Pegasus Telematic University

Amelia Manuti, University of Bari Aldo Moro

Modern workplaces face significant transformation driven by technology and changing organizational structures, requiring continuous competence development. While formal training and informal learning have been extensively studied separately, evidence shows their boundaries blur and features coexist in practice. This special issue seeks empirical research on various forms of workplace learning and their contributions to sustainable professional development.

The special issue welcomes studies examining formal and informal learning relationships, hybrid practices like mentoring and peer learning, training transfer, technology-mediated approaches, contextual factors influencing learning, intergenerational knowledge sharing, and connections between learning and outcomes such as well-being and career sustainability. Research should adopt diverse methodologies across different occupational and cultural contexts.

Appel publié par Journal of Workplace Learning. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Formal and informal learning
  • Training transfer
  • Informal workplace learning
  • Technology-mediated learning
  • Learning across generations
  • Workplace learning and career development
  • Learning and sustainable outcomes
